whatThisFileIs: An R1 authorship claim for the AFC-250 change: land the retention_job credential policy of AFC-244 as a credential inventory document, point repo-plan §6 at it, and set rolconnlimit = 1 on retention_job in bootstrap. The CTO (MediaTech) is the author of all four paths. R2 does not apply to these paths -- REVIEW_REQUIRED_PATHS covers engine/**, migrations/**, tests/db/** and two scripts, and deliberately does not cover services/directus/schema/bootstrap/** (recorded as finding F6 of the CTO verdict on AFC-244). The commit still requires a second reviewer under docs/planning/repo-plan.md §line 68 ('Critical paths (auth, permissions, data migrations) require a second reviewer (CTO or SecurityEngineer)'): the author is the CTO, so the reviewer is SecurityEngineer, and that review is requested as a child issue of AFC-250 before this commit lands. A `reviews[]` entry with the review issue and verdict will be added to this file at commit time.
basis: AFC-250 lands the decision of record saved on AFC-244 (document key `decision`). Part 1 of the issue is the CTO item-by-item review verdict on that decision, posted as a comment on AFC-244: the three-credential inventory is accepted with a scope finding (F1: §0 claims 'credentials that exist in this company' but the estate also names POSTGRES_PASSWORD, DIRECTUS_ADMIN_PASSWORD and EMAIL_SMTP_PASSWORD; §1 landed exactly as decided and the gap is recorded in the artefact rather than silently expanded), the 90/180 split is upheld (erasure is irreversible, so the erase-capable credential gets half the exposure window; the unaligned schedules cost two rotation events a year and buy per-credential attribution), the five triggers are upheld with F3 (a trigger with no detector is a procedure: the only mechanical detector in the company is the AFC-251 static gate, which is itself blocked, so trigger 1 currently has zero mechanical coverage and nothing scans Paperclip threads), owner=CTO/reviewer=SecurityEngineer is upheld with F4 (independence verified by access, not by seat: SecurityEngineer holds no secret binding and no cluster access), and both section 4 rulings are upheld with corrected premises -- §4.1 rolvaliduntil stays NULL because retention_last_run_at is a column nobody is paged on (the alarm exists only as a view COMMENT; infra-spec wires no such alert), and §4.2 rolconnlimit = 1 stands because the engine's pg_try_advisory_lock bounds runs while rolconnlimit bounds sessions, the lock being re-entrant within one session. Part 2 of the issue is the artefact: docs/security/credential-inventory.md carries the six required elements, repo-plan §6 now points at it instead of restating it, and bootstrap sets and asserts the connection limit. The change was verified by a negative control run against a fresh PGlite with the real bootstrap file applied (retention_job = 1, other three roles still -1, rolvaliduntil NULL on all four; the assertion passes on the clean state, refuses 2 and 0 with sqlstate 23001, and passes after repair; re-running bootstrap converges a drifted 7 back to 1) and by pnpm test:db before and after the change (16 suites / 564 assertions / 0 failing, identical to baseline).
verificationRecorded: BASELINE (before touching the file): node scripts/run-db-tests.mjs -> 16 suites / 564 assertions / 0 failing; pnpm gate:self-test, gate:awareness, gate:retention, gate:migration-privilege and gate:rollback-control all exit 0. POST-CHANGE: identical 16 suites / 564 assertions / 0 failing, and the same five gates exit 0. pnpm test exits 1 at exactly one failure, gate:adr-uniqueness, and it fails IDENTICALLY before and after this change: two tracked docs/adr/ADR-0006-*.md files claim the same ADR number, work owned by AFC-271 (an issue assigned to the CTO but blocked pending an engine/** citation fix that is itself an R2 file needing a reviewer). That red is recorded as an adverse AC6 finding on AFC-250 rather than fixed here, because fixing it would mean editing R2 paths inside an issue whose own change is not yet reviewed. NEGATIVE CONTROL: a scratch script applied services/directus/schema/bootstrap/0001_roles.sql to a fresh PGlite, read pg_roles and pg_auth_members, then drove the new assertion through the pass/refuse/repair cases described in `basis`; the script lived under the run's PAPERCLIP_SCRATCH_DIR and was never committed. PASSWORD SCAN (AC4): no `ALTER ROLE ... PASSWORD` for any of the four roles anywhere in the repository, no quoted password value for them, and services/directus/.env.example carries empty values only; the only literal found is the application dev stub STUB_PASSWORD = 'stub-not-a-secret' in an app file and UI labels, neither of which is a credential. The inventory document itself contains no password material: the rotation procedure is written as bare `ALTER ROLE retention_job WITH PASSWORD` with no value.
